description: Target mode: a request whose forwarded header value holds a NUL byte cannot be carried by a web Request / HTTP client, and is answered 400 {"error":"request cannot be represented as a web Request"} without contacting the local server, the same reply as in handler mode, never a 500 or a 502. MCPWARP.md §4.5
in:
POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: notes-tester.mcpwarp.test
accept: application/json, text/event-stream
content-type: application/json
user-agent: Go-http-client/1.1
x-bad: a�b
Content-Length: 40

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}
out:
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 58

{"error":"request cannot be represented as a web Request"}
notes: NUL is the one byte every SDK's request type rejects (fetch Headers, Rust http::HeaderValue, Go net/http, Python's NUL/CR/LF check); other control bytes are runtime-dependent and not pinned. The body is read before the reply, as for any request that reaches row 6 of §4.4.
